options.title: Could the Sahara turn green again?
options.first_line: Could the Sahara, the biggest hot desert on Earth, turn green again?
options.first_frame: The old map of North Africa, the Sahara's sand colour across eleven countries, a green tide already creeping up from its southern edge.

options.title: The Sahara used to be green. Why?
options.first_line: The Sahara, the biggest hot desert on Earth, used to be green grassland. So could it turn green again?
options.first_frame: Sand-coloured North Africa on the map flickering to green and back, a small hippo standing in the middle of the dunes.

options.title: What if the Sahara became grassland?
options.first_line: What if the Sahara, the biggest hot desert on Earth, became grassland and lakes overnight?
options.first_frame: North Africa on the map, a big lake filling in the middle of the desert and grass spreading out from its shore.

why: A hippo standing in desert dunes is a surprise you get with the sound off, and 'used to be green. Why?' opens a how-is-that-possible question the title doesn't answer, so you have to stay for it.
